source_text: Sed quoniam edidimus, antiquissimis Judaeorum instrumentis sectam istam esse suffultam, quam aliquanto novellam, ut Tiberiani temporis, plerique sciunt, profitentibus nobis quoque; fortasse an hoc nomine de statu ejus retractetur, quasi sub umbraculo insignissimae religionis, certe licitae, aliquid propriae praesumptionis abscondat, vel quia praeter aetatem neque de victus exceptionibus, neque de solemnitatibus dierum, neque de ipso signaculo corporis, neque de consortio nominis cum Judaeis agimus, quod utique oporteret, si eidem Deo manciparemur? Sed et vulgus jam scit Christum, hominem utique aliquem, qualem Judaei judicaverunt, quo facilius quis nos hominis cultores existimaverit. Verum neque de Christo erubescimus, quum sub nomine ejus deputari et damnari juvat, neque de deo aliter praesumimus. Necesse est igitur pauca dicamus de Christo ut Deo. Tantum Judaeis erat apud Deum gratia, ubi et insignis justitia et fides originalium auctorum, unde illis et generis magnitudo et regni sublimitas floruit et tanta felicitas, ut Dei vocibus, quibus edocebantur, de promerendo Deo, et non offendendo, praemonerentur. Sed quanta deliquerint, fiducia patrum inflati [ad delirandum], derivantes a disciplina in profanum modum, etsi ipsi non confiterentur, probaret exitus hodiernus ipsorum. Dispersi, palabundi, et coeli et soli sui extorres, vagantur per orbem, sine homine, sine Deo rege, quibus nec advenarum jure terram patriam saltem vestigio salutare conceditur. Cum haec illis sanctae voces praeminarentur, eaedem fere semper omnes ingerebant fore, uti sub extimis curriculis saeculi ex omni jam gente, et populo, et loco cultores sibi allegeret Deus multo fideliores, in quos gratiam transferret, et pleniorem quidem ob disciplinae auctioris capacitatem. [Venit igitur, qui ad reformandam et illuminandam eam venturus a Deo praenuntiabatur, Christus ille Filius dei]. Hujus igitur gratiae disciplinaeque arbiter et magister, illuminator atque deductor generis humani, Filius Dei annuntiabatur, non quidem ita genitus, ut erubescat de filii nomine aut de patris semine;
pass_a_gloss: But because we have stated that this sect is supported by the most ancient instruments of the Jews, which many know to be rather new, from the time of Tiberius, and we also profess; perhaps for this reason it is retracted from its status, as if under the shade of a most famous and certainly permitted religion, it hides some presumption of its own, or because beyond age we do not deal with exceptions of food, or solemnities of days, or the very sign of the body, or the sharing of the name with Jews, which certainly would be necessary if we were to be devoted to the same God. But the crowd already knows Christ, a man indeed, such as the Jews judged, so that anyone may easily think us to be worshippers of a man. But we are not ashamed of Christ, since it is beneficial to be assigned and condemned under his name, nor do we presume otherwise about God. It is necessary, therefore, to say a few things about Christ as God. The Jews had so much grace with God, where there was also notable justice and faith of the original authors, from which they had greatness of race and sublimity of kingdom, and so much happiness, that they were warned by God's voices, by which they were taught, about deserving God and not offending him. But how much they have sinned, puffed up by confidence in their fathers to the point of madness, deviating from discipline into a profane manner, even if they themselves do not confess, their current outcome proves. Dispersed, wandering, and banished from both heaven and their own sun, they wander through the world, without a man, without a king God, to whom not even the right of strangers is granted to greet their native land with a footstep. When holy voices foretold these things to them, they almost always inserted that God would choose for himself worshippers much more faithful from every nation, people, and place, to whom he would transfer his grace, and more full indeed because of the greater capacity of discipline. Therefore, the one who was to come to reform and illuminate, foretold by God, came, Christ the Son of God. Therefore, the Son of God was announced as the arbiter and master of this grace and discipline, the illuminator and leader of the human race, not born in such a way that he is ashamed of the name of son or the seed of the Father;

choices.english: we are not ashamed of Christ
rejected: nor are we ashamed of Christ

pass_b_english: We have shown that the earliest Jewish writings back this sect, even though most people know it only dates to Tiberius’ reign and we ourselves claim it. Perhaps that is why its legal standing is challenged—as if, sheltering under the shade of a famous and certainly permitted religion, it were concealing some presumption of its own, or because, apart from its youth, we share none of the Jewish food restrictions, holy days, bodily sign, or common name that would be required if we served the same God. The public already knows Christ as a man—exactly the kind the Jews condemned—so it is easy to assume we worship a mere human. Yet we are not ashamed of Christ, since it serves us to be identified and condemned under his name, and we make no other presumption about God. We must therefore say a few things about Christ as God.

The Jews once enjoyed such grace with God that their founding fathers’ remarkable justice and faith produced national greatness, royal splendor, and immense prosperity; God’s own voices warned them how to merit his favor and avoid offending him. But see how far they fell: puffed up by ancestral pride to the point of madness, they abandoned discipline for profanity, and even if they will not admit it, their present condition proves the charge. Scattered, homeless, exiled from both heaven and their native sun, they wander the world without a leader, without a divine King, not even granted a stranger’s right to set foot in their homeland. When holy voices foretold this fate, those same voices almost always added that God would gather far more faithful worshippers from every nation, people, and place, transfer his grace to them, and give it in fuller measure because their discipline would have greater capacity. So the One who was to come to reform and illuminate, foretold by God, arrived—Christ the Son of God. Therefore the Son of God was proclaimed arbiter and master of this grace and discipline, illuminator and guide of the human race, not born in a way that would make him ashamed of the name Son or of the Father’s seed.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause translation, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the theological nuances and agency of the original. All specific details regarding the Jewish 'instruments', the comparison to Tiberius's time, the list of differences (food, days, sign, name), and the description of the Jewish diaspora are preserved. The distinction between Christ as man (as judged by Jews) and Christ as God is correctly maintained. No omissions or contradictions found.

source_identity: 'Sed quoniam edidimus, antiquissimis Judaeorum instrumentis sectam istam esse suffultam, quam aliquanto novellam, ut Tiberiani temporis, plerique sciunt, profitentibus nobis quoque;' (Latin), 'But because we have stated that this sect is supported by the most ancient instruments of the Jews, which many know to be rather new, from the time of Tiberius, and we also profess;' (Pass A); 'We have shown that the earliest Jewish writings back this sect, even though most people know it only dates to Tiberius’ reign and we ourselves claim it.' (Pass B). completeness: All clauses from the Latin are reflected in Pass A and B. negation: 'neque de Christo erubescimus' is rendered as 'we are not ashamed of Christ' in both Pass A and B. agency: 'Filius Dei annuntiabatur' is rendered as 'the Son of God was proclaimed' in Pass B. modality: 'Necesse est igitur pauca dicamus de Christo ut Deo' is rendered as 'It is necessary, therefore, to say a few things about Christ as God' in Pass A. doctrine: 'Christus ille Filius dei' is rendered as 'Christ the Son of God' in both Pass A and B. scripture: No scripture citations are present in the text.
